title: refactor: shard-lint-executor-by-language-and-add-release-quarantine-hook
author: Priya Natarajan
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic lint executor has grown slow and brittle as we added language-specific rules and formatters. This PR splits the lint runner into language-aware shards (js/ts, python, go, docs) so presubmit latency improves on common change types and tooling installs are scoped.

What this does (single-line description + checklist):
- Introduces a small lint-shard runner binary (go) that fans out to language workers based on changed paths and manifest hints.
- Adds a release-quarantine gate in release automation: PRs that touch release/*, changelog, or package manifests must pass a release metadata validation job before merge.
- Moves heavy toolchain bootstrap steps into optional per-shard init steps so the default fastpath avoids installing rust/cargo/golang for JS-only changes.
- Updates CI templates and local dev shim to retain backward compatibility for local docker-based runs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Split runner and add per-language job manifests
- [x] Add release-quarantine check and validator script
- [x] Update GH Action templates and workflow matrix to use shard hints
- [x] Add docs for contributors (CONTRIBUTING.md additions)
- [x] Smoke-tested on staging branch

Related context: ENG-1182 tracks presubmit latency for js-only PRs; ENG-1199 is the release automation hardening work triggered by a missed release-note incident (SUP-3421). This change is intentionally conservative: default behavior is unchanged unless shard hints or path globs indicate a language-specific fastpath.

Notes on backwards compatibility and migration: The old monolithic lint action remains available under workflows/legacy-lint.yml for two weeks and is removed in a follow-up cleanup. The new shard runner will log telemetry (metric: ci.lint.shard_hit) to help tune default shard mappings.

Runtime/operational notes: The shard runner is small (stateless) and can be packaged into the existing actions/runner image. The release-quarantine hook runs as a required check on release branches; it validates presence of release metadata and verifies release note format. Failure causes an explicit blocking status and a short human-readable remediation hint.
commits:
1) introduce lint-shard runner and per-language manifests
2) wire GH Actions workflows to use shard hints and path filters
3) add release-quarantine validator and action wrapper
4) update CONTRIBUTING.md and workflow docs
5) add telemetry hooks and fallback to legacy runner

(5 commits, authored by Priya Natarajan)
review_thread:
Ethan Cole: Overall clean split, thanks. Two concerns: 1) matcher.go uses a new path heuristic — add unit tests for ambiguous globs; 2) release validator must treat maintenance branches differently.

Priya Natarajan: Added unit tests for matcher edge cases and updated validator to allow 'maintenance/*' branches to bypass quarantine when tagged with 'chore/release-skip' label.

Marta Ruiz: Can we gate installing Python formatters behind your shard init step? Some flaky installs were observed in the staging runs.

Priya Natarajan: Yes — moved heavy installers to per-shard init and made the default fastpath skip pip installs for non-python shards. Verified with staged CI run.

Noah Zhang: Approving after minor nits on docs and one lint rule that accidentally drifted into go lint manifest.

Merge notes: Squash merge used. Legacy workflow kept temporarily. Telemetry flagged for 48h monitoring.
release_notes: Splits lint executor into language-aware shards to reduce presubmit latency and adds a release-quarantine validation check to block merges missing release metadata. Legacy lint workflow retained temporarily. See CONTRIBUTING.md for contributor notes.
